scope: Historical Mode data for World War I, World War II, postwar treaties, League of Nations and country-level fatality estimates. This is research data, not yet an engine import contract.

ww1.endMeaning: Western Front armistice; Central Powers ceased fighting on separate dates. Treaty of Versailles was signed 1919-06-28 and is not the war end date.

ww2.endMeaning: Germany's surrender took effect 8 May 1945 (9 May in Moscow); Japan signed the Instrument of Surrender 2 September 1945. China-Japan war began 1937-07-07 and is represented as a prelude theatre.

wars.name: World War I / Great War
wars.startEvent: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, following the July Crisis.
wars.endEvent: Compiègne Armistice signed 1918-11-11; fighting ceased at 11:00 CET on the Western Front. Separate armistices: Bulgaria 1918-09-29; Ottoman Empire 1918-10-30; Austria-Hungary 1918-11-03. Treaty of Brest-Litovsk removed Soviet Russia from the war on 1918-03-03.

members.name: Russian Empire
members.note: Bolshevik government signed Brest-Litovsk; do not use 1917 revolution date as the legal end of the war.

members.name: United Kingdom / British Empire
members.note: Colonial and Dominion forces are included in imperial casualty sources; do not double count them as separate sovereign belligerents.

members.name: Kingdom of Montenegro
members.note: Montenegro capitulated in January 1916; government-in-exile and later military formations complicate a single exit date.

members.name: Portuguese Republic
members.note: Formal German declaration followed Portuguese seizure of German ships; Portuguese forces had been deployed earlier.

members.name: Kingdom of Romania
members.note: Treaty of Bucharest 1918; Romania re-entered the war on 1918-11-10, one day before the general armistice.

sideChanges.name: Romania re-entered the war shortly before the general armistice.

members.name: Kingdom of Greece
members.note: National Schism: pro-Allied government declared war; exact legal entry date is given as 27 June 1917 in standard chronologies.

members.name: United States of America
members.note: Congress declared war on Germany 6 April 1917; declaration against Austria-Hungary followed 7 December 1917.

members.name: Republic of China
members.note: Declared war on Germany and Austria-Hungary; Chinese Labour Corps service predates the declaration.

members.name: Kingdom of Siam
members.note: CoW historical code SIA; modern ISO3 is THA.

members.name: Republic of Liberia
members.note: Declared war on Germany; limited direct combat participation.

members.name: German Empire
members.note: CoW historical code GMY.

members.name: Austria-Hungary
members.note: Villa Giusti Armistice; the Habsburg monarchy dissolved in November 1918.

members.name: Ottoman Empire
members.note: Armistice of Mudros; Ottoman state did not sign the final 1919 Treaty of Sèvres until the later postwar settlement.

members.name: Kingdom of Bulgaria
members.note: Armistice of Salonica.

wars.name: World War II
wars.startEvent: Germany invaded Poland on 1939-09-01; United Kingdom and France declared war on Germany on 1939-09-03.
wars.endEvent: German surrender signed at Reims 1945-05-07 and Berlin 1945-05-08; effective 1945-05-08 23:01 CET. Japan formally signed surrender on 1945-09-02.

prelude.note: Second Sino-Japanese War is treated as a major prelude/theatre of the wider conflict; the conventional global-war start remains 1939-09-01.

members.name: Second Polish Republic
members.note: The Polish state was occupied; government-in-exile and armed forces continued with the Allies through the end of the global war.

members.name: United Kingdom and British Empire
members.note: Dominions and India had distinct constitutional declarations/status; do not collapse all imperial forces into one population record.

members.name: French Republic / Free France
members.capital: Paris (Vichy government at Vichy after 1940; Free French provisional capital Algiers then Paris)
members.note: Armistice of 22 June 1940 ended the Third Republic's active campaign; Free France continued fighting. Treat Vichy and Free France as distinct political authorities, not as a clean French exit from the Allied war.

sideChanges.name: Free France under Charles de Gaulle continued the war after the armistice; represent Vichy and Free France as separate authorities where supported.

members.name: Nepal
members.note: Nepal declared war on Germany in September 1939; not an independent UN-style declaration chronology.

members.name: Kingdom of the Netherlands
members.note: Germany invaded the Netherlands on 10 May 1940; the government continued from London.

members.name: Kingdom of Belgium
members.note: Germany invaded Belgium on 10 May 1940; the Belgian Army capitulated on 28 May, while the government and forces in exile continued Allied participation.

members.name: Kingdom of Norway
members.note: Norwegian forces in exile and merchant fleet continued for the Allies.

members.name: Kingdom of Greece
members.note: Greek government and forces continued in exile after mainland surrender.

members.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
members.note: Royal government and resistance continued; partisan-led Yugoslavia became a major Allied belligerent.

members.name: Republic of China
members.note: War with Japan began in 1937; China is the key pre-1939 theatre exception.

members.name: United States of America
members.note: Declared war on Japan 8 Dec 1941; Germany and Italy declared war on the USA on 11 Dec 1941.

members.name: Kingdom of Italy (Fascist regime)

sideChanges.name: Kingdom of Italy declared war on Germany; co-belligerent with the Allies.

members.note: Italian Social Republic in the north remained aligned with Germany; model post-armistice Italy as split authorities if the engine supports it.

members.name: Empire of Japan
members.note: Second Sino-Japanese War began in 1937; formal global-war chronology begins 1939.

members.name: Kingdom of Hungary
members.note: Armistice signed 20 Jan 1945 by the provisional government; German occupation and Arrow Cross regime continued fighting.

sideChanges.name: King Michael's coup; Romania ceased fighting the USSR and turned against Germany. Armistice signed 12 Sep 1944.

members.name: Kingdom of Bulgaria

sideChanges.name: Bulgaria declared war on Germany after Soviet forces entered; armistice with Allies signed 28 Oct 1944.

members.note: Bulgaria joined the Axis Tripartite Pact 1 Mar 1941, declared war on Britain and the USA in Dec 1941, but did not declare war on the USSR before the Soviet invasion in Sep 1944.

members.name: Slovak Republic (1939–1945)
members.note: The Slovak Republic participated in the invasion of Poland as a German satellite; formal Axis alignment followed later.

members.name: Republic of Finland (co-belligerent)
members.note: Finland fought the USSR alongside Germany but was not a signatory to the Tripartite Pact; Moscow Armistice 19 Sep 1944; Lapland War against Germany began 15 Sep 1944.

members.name: Kingdom of Thailand
members.note: Declared war on Britain and the USA; the Thai ambassador in Washington did not deliver the declaration to the US government, and the Free Thai movement resisted Japanese control.

members.name: Albania (under Italian then German occupation)
members.note: Not a fully sovereign Axis partner throughout; the status field prevents treating occupation as a normal sovereign declaration.

unitedStates.note: The US signed the Covenant as part of the Treaty of Versailles but the Senate did not ratify the treaty; the United States never joined the League.

membership.note: The Covenant Annex separates original signatories from states invited to accede. The annex is not a safe substitute for a dated membership ledger: some accessions took effect later, and the League reached 63 members over its life.

permanentMembers.note: Italy announced withdrawal in 1937; two-year notice period under Covenant Article 1.
Japan notified withdrawal in 1933; two-year notice period.
Permanent Council status approved September 1926; withdrawal notice October 1933.
Permanent Council status in 1934; expelled after attack on Finland.

council.earlyYearsCaveat: 1920–1925 exact non-permanent composition by calendar year is not fully reconstructed in this staging file; only initial members and seat-count changes are asserted. 1926–1939 table is transcribed from a published institutional-history study based on League Official Journal records.
council.unanimity: Covenant Article 5: decisions of Assembly and Council generally required agreement of all members represented, except matters of procedure and express exceptions. Article 15 has a dispute-report exception excluding parties to the dispute from the unanimity calculation.

withdrawalsAndExpulsion.note: Expulsion followed the Soviet attack on Finland; this was not a voluntary withdrawal.

casualties.method: Use ranges and preserve source-specific estimates. Military deaths are not identical to battle deaths; civilian estimates may include famine, disease, genocide, occupation and postwar mortality depending on source. Never sum incompatible source series into one false-precision total.

ww1.note: Reliable civilian split not provided in the sources selected; mark unverified rather than infer.
Civilian deaths, including Armenian genocide and famine, are not harmonized in the cited series; no single number asserted.

ww2.note: Museum source gives 24 million total; civilian interval here is a residual range and should be treated as derived/approximate, not an independent census.
The museum explicitly warns some estimates exceed 50 million total; use the cited 20m as a conservative baseline, not settled consensus.

integrationWarnings: This staging dataset does not assert that all belligerents in all theatres are covered; it contains principal belligerents and selected formal declarations. A future exhaustive pass should add colonial forces, governments-in-exile, resistance forces and all minor declarations.
Capital strings are historical city names, not engine region IDs. Resolve them through the actual region registry and record a mapping confidence before engine use.
WWI and WWII dates describe legal entry, armistice, surrender or campaign end depending on the participant; these event types must not be collapsed into a single boolean.
WWII France, Poland, Belgium, Norway and Greece continued Allied belligerency after metropolitan capitulation; do not remove their governments-in-exile or armed forces from the Allied side.

Italy, Romania and Bulgaria require side-switch events. Finland was a co-belligerent with Germany against the USSR, not a formal Axis Pact member. Bulgaria's wartime relationship with the USSR is exceptional.

Sèvres was not ratified/implemented as written; Lausanne superseded it. Yalta and Potsdam were conference protocols, not comprehensive peace treaties. San Francisco 1951 renounced claims but often did not specify a recipient state.
The League Covenant Annex is a signatory/accession list, not a complete dated membership register. The 1920–1925 Council elected-member sequence remains partly unverified in this version.
WWI civilian deaths are especially uncertain and sometimes include famine, disease or influenza. WW2 casualty estimates vary substantially; source series have different definitions and boundaries.

The treaty-to-region entries are historical place names only. No automatic transfer should run until Claude matches each name against the engine region registry and checks date, sovereignty and successor-state rules.
